object_description: a large house framed by two low wings around a central garden
design_condition: The U-shaped complex occupies three plot edges, leaving a central garden connected to the castle park, while its low wings and placement along the historic boundaries respond to the slope, village, orchard, and castle.

positive.statement: The concept of the large house is plausible as a village-related volume and a sign of welcome.
The dining room and the sequence from covered indoor terrace to outdoor terrace are high-quality spaces.
Placing the entire accommodation program on one level is a positive aspect of the proposal.
The rooms’ relationship to the garden and landscape is well established, with privacy managed through successive thresholds.
The historical issue is placed at the heart of the project, restoring the legibility of the monument and landscape.
The modest elevation and flat green roof of the southeast wing contribute to good integration into the countryside.
The eastern walk connects existing and new paths and highlights western landscape views through belvedere squares.
The protected central garden is welcoming and invites residents to wander.

negative.statement: The entirely vertical distribution of common functions over four levels poses a usage problem for residents.
The limited clearance on the street is unsatisfactory as an EMS forecourt and village interface.
The one-level accommodation bias creates a large built footprint on the site.
The transformation toward military fort architecture with palisades is surprising and historically erroneous.
The historic park is reduced because the orchard and vegetable garden largely disappear.
The central garden establishes few relationships with the existing wooded park.
The western facade remains essentially uninhabited despite the proposed fruit-tree alignment.
